summary: Guidance requested: shard-aware idempotency strategy for multiplexed tool chains across Go/TS SDKs
description:
Issue summary:
NimbusPayments is implementing a high-throughput payment-validation workflow that orchestrates three external tools in sequence (risk-check, account-lookup, settlement-prep). They use multiplexed client connections and the TS client on the web front-end plus a Go worker pool for server-side orchestration. They are asking for best-practice guidance for designing an idempotency strategy that avoids collisions and duplicate tool-side effects when requests are sharded across multiple worker processes and both SDKs are used.

Impact:
- Potential duplicate downstream charges or duplicate webhook posts observed in a narrow subset of high-concurrency runs (approx 0.01% of transactions).
- Customer is hesitant to roll to 100% for a dedicated flow because of regulatory payout concerns.

What they want:
- Concrete, shard-aware idempotency key design patterns that work when requests are rebalanced between workers, when streaming reconnects occur, and when some calls are retried at the orchestration layer.
- SDK compatibility notes: how to ensure Go and TS SDKs generate equivalent idempotency identifiers and headers.

Observed behavior:
- Customer currently derives idempotency keys using: sha1(truncate(payload_json, 1024) + tool_name + user_id) then base64-url-encode and sets header X-Redwood-Idempotency.
- Under heavy load with the Go worker pool (20 workers, multiplexing on a single HTTP/2 connection) they see occasional duplicate tool invocations when a worker is restarted and the orchestration retry replays.
- Duplicates correlate with requests that were routed to a different worker shard (same client session) within ~45s of original execution.

Customer configuration details:
- Dedicated pool: 8x A100s per shard, autoscaled by queue depth.
- Go worker pool uses per-process in-memory idempotency cache with TTL 60s. No shared cache.
- TS frontend sends requests via the Redwood hosted API to the dedicated pool and attaches same X-Redwood-Idempotency header value computed in client JS.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a Go worker pool with 4 processes handling multiplexed requests (http2).
2) Use the current deterministic key: truncated(sha1(payload))+tool_name+user_id base64-url header from both TS and Go clients.
3) Simulate burst: 5k similar requests/sec targeting same small set of user_ids, force a worker restart for one process mid-burst (SIGTERM) to cause reroute and replay.
4) Observe downstream tool webhook logs for duplicate invocations within 2 minutes of the original run.

comments: 2026-03-12T15:05 Diego Martinez: Thanks for the clear reproduction notes, Ava. Initial thought: per-process in-memory cache is the weak link here. If a worker restarts the cache is lost and the server will see a replay as new unless the request-level idempotency header maps to a shared store or is checked against a persistent dedup table.

2026-03-12T15:22 Ava Chen: Customer asked whether increasing TTL to 5 minutes will be safe. They worry about poisoning dedup state for legitimate replays across retries. Also asked about namespace/shard-prefixing best practices so multiple workers can co-exist without collisions.

2026-03-12T16:10 SRE (Priya Rao): Adding notes from infra — dedicated pools have an optional Redis-backed dedup store (internal flag dedup_store=on). We should confirm whether the SDKs support attaching a shard id or a monotonic sequence to the idempotency key and whether we have library helpers documented.
investigation: 2026-03-12T17:00 Diego Martinez: Reproduced locally with stress harness. When worker cache is in-memory only, a restart causes duplicates. When switching to a shared Redis dedup store with strict write-once semantics for (idempotency_key -> terminal_status) duplicates disappear in test cluster.

2026-03-12T17:30 Diego Martinez: Observed that the customer's JS helper was trimming non-ASCII characters before hashing while Go used binary protobuf bytes directly — this can produce mismatched hashes if payload canonicalization differs. Recommended canonical JSON (utf-8 normalization NFC) prior to hash.

2026-03-12T18:05 Priya Rao: Checked dedicated pool metrics and found a small window (~30–90s) where autoscaler rebalances and reconnects caused in-flight requests to be replayed. With per-process cache TTL < 120s those replays escape the dedup window.
resolution:
Temporary workaround provided: enable our Redis-backed dedup_store for the affected dedicated pool and increase TTL to 5 minutes while they complete rollout. Provided a canonicalization checklist for keys: (1) normalize payload JSON to canonical ordering and NFC unicode, (2) include tool_name + user_id + operator-shard-id as explicit components before hashing, (3) use sha256 and base64url encode without truncation.

Long-term recommended solution: adopt a shard-aware key: prefix keys with a deterministic shard id OR use a global request UUID generated by the orchestrator and propagated to all SDKs (recommended). We opened an internal task to add a lightweight helper in both SDKs that exposes a canonical idempotency_key builder for multi-language parity.

Follow-ups created: INT-3321 to add SDK helper; docs PR requested: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/210; customer confirmed workaround reduces duplicates in staging after enabling dedup_store.
resolution_status: Workaround applied; awaiting SDK helper and docs
follow_up_actions: INT-3321: Add canonical idempotency key builder to sdk-ts and sdk-go (owner: Diego)
DOC-210: Update best-practices page with shard-aware patterns and canonicalization checklist
SRE-flag: Recommend enabling dedup_store by default for dedicated pools handling financial flows
